items.q: Elderly with drusen, pigment clumping and bent lines but no blood is which stage and managed how?
o: Intermediate dry AMD; AREDS2 with smoking stop and monitoring
items.exp: Large soft drusen with pigment change risk conversion; supplements slow some while Amsler and OCT catch wet turn early. No injections help dry disease.
items.kp: Drusen plus bent lines, no blood: dry, supplement.

items.q: Sudden central distortion with subretinal blood in 75 year old needs what urgently?
o: Anti VEGF injections after OCT angiography confirmation of wet AMD
items.exp: Choroidal vessels bleed beneath fovea scarring disciform within weeks; loading injections dry rapidly while delay wastes reading vision permanently.
items.kp: Blood under old macula: inject this week.

items.q: Watzke Allen slit sign with full thickness foveal defect on OCT is what and treated how?
o: Macular hole; vitrectomy with membrane peel and face down gas
items.exp: Vitreous traction punches fovea open; peeling with tamponade closes most while posturing compliance decides. Lamellar defects differ, observing.
items.kp: Broken light slit at centre: hole needs gas.

items.q: Cellophane reflex with metamorphosia and intact outer layers on OCT is what?
o: Epiretinal membrane observing until reading fails then peel
items.exp: Glial membrane wrinkles inner retina bending lines; surgery when acuity or distortion disrupts function while mild cases watch. Cataract coexists commonly.

items.q: Beaten bronze macula with pisciform flecks in teenager with recessive inheritance is what?
items.exp: Lipofuscin flecks carpet posterior pole blurring centre in youth; sun protection with low vision aids bridges while vitamin A excess avoided and trials watched.

items.q: Egg yolk macular lesion with abnormal EOG and normal ERG in child is which dystrophy?
items.exp: Bestrophin disrupts pigment epithelium pumping (light rise lost on EOG); yolk scrambles then scars slowly while complications (new vessels) treat selectively.
items.kp: Egg yolk centre with bad EOG: Best.

items.q: Lacquer cracks with Fuchs spot in highly myopic eye signal what risk?
o: Myopic choroidal new vessels needing anti VEGF with surveillance
items.exp: Bruch cracks invite membranes bleeding beneath elongated macula; injections dry while posterior staphyloma watches detachments. Glasses never treat membranes.
items.kp: Cracked myopic macula bleeding: inject membranes.

items.q: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy is distinguished and treated how?
o: Branching network with polyps on indocyanine green; photodynamic with anti VEGF
items.exp: Asian variant bleeds massively with orange nodules; combined therapy closes polyps while anti VEGF alone underperforms. Indocyanine maps networks.
items.kp: Orange polyps bleeding: light plus inject.

items.q: Solar maculopathy after eclipse gazing shows what and counselled how?
o: Foveal photoreceptor burn with central scotoma; prevention with certified filters, observation
items.exp: Photochemical burn holes outer segments permanently in proportion to gaze; no therapy restores while filters prevent recurrence. Welders share risk.
items.kp: Eclipse stare, central blind spot: burnt fovea.

items.q: Geographic atrophy in advanced dry AMD is managed chiefly how?
o: Low vision aids with complement inhibition debates; no injections restore
items.exp: Sharply punched chorioretinal loss expands slowly despite supplements; magnification, lighting and rehabilitation sustain function while trials test complement blockade.
items.kp: Map like atrophy: magnify, do not inject.
